newsitem.title: POLAND: GM unit to invest $38 mln in Poland by 2001.
newsitem.headline: GM unit to invest $38 mln in Poland by 2001.

text.p: The U.S. Delphi Automotive Systems, a unit of General Motors Corp plans to invest $38 million in a car accessories factory in a special economic zone in southern Poland, the zone's official said on Tuesday.

Wlodzimierz Zak told Reuters a Polish firm Delphi Polska Automotive Systems sp z oo, 100-percent owned by U.S. Delphi had already paid 2.7 million zlotys for buildings in the zone and said the factory was likely to employ 200.

"The total investments will amount to $38 million by 2001," he said, added that eight million of the sum would be earmarked for buildings and land purchase and $30 million for the factory's equipment.

Germany's Adam Opel AG, a GM subsidiary is about to start construction of its 500 million mark car factory to employ 2,000, located in the southern town of Gliwice. It is due to be completed by the end of 1998.
